name: Secret RF
lead: Secret RF is a fractional microneedling radiofrequency device made by Cutera and used in aesthetic medicine to improve skin quality and reduce facial wrinkles. A clinician passes a handpiece with fine needles over the face; people seek it for smoother texture, firmer-looking skin and softer lines.[2][3]

Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny sterile needles puncture the skin repeatedly to prompt a healing response, and it has been used for scarring and acne with research ongoing; devices that add radiofrequency energy through the needles are a variant of the approach.[1]
Published information on Secret RF specifically is limited to two clinical trial registrations from 2018, one for skin quality and one for facial wrinkles.[2][3]
infobox: Skin quality, facial wrinkles (per registered studies)

paras: The device combines microneedling with radiofrequency energy, a category of in-clinic skin rejuvenation treatments. Microneedling procedures generally involve repeated skin punctures that prompt the body's repair response.[1]

The microneedling article reports that its main safety concern is infection risk when procedures are done in non-medical settings by people untrained in infection control, and notes an April 2024 CDC report of HIV diagnoses in three women after vampire facials at a New Mexico spa; that report concerned microneedling with platelet-rich plasma rather than RF devices.[1]

A multi-center clinical evaluation of the Cutera Secret RF device (27 participants, condition listed as skin quality) started in January 2018 and is listed as completed.[2] A separate 40-participant study of the Secret micro-needle fractional RF system for facial wrinkles started in February 2018; its status is listed as unknown.[3] Outcome results from these registrations were not found.

timeline.event: Two registered studies of Secret RF begin.[2][3]

quick.overview:
Secret RF is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device from Cutera, used in clinics for skin quality and facial wrinkles.

Two trials were registered in 2018; results are not summarized here.
quick.mechanism: Fine needles enter the skin and deliver RF energy in a fractional pattern, with the intended aim of stimulating remodeling.
quick.risks: Device-specific safety data are not covered here. General microneedling carries infection risk when performed without proper infection control.

chain: Needles with radiofrequency energy treat the skin
Smoother texture and softer wrinkles are the intended result
angle.text: Patients have the treatment in a clinic to improve texture and fine lines. The two registered studies of the device list skin quality and facial wrinkles as the conditions under evaluation.
